The brainstorming skill applies to "creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior" - this is not that; it's a mechanical test action the user explicitly requested.

The Edit tool requires reading the file first in this conversation, or the call will fail. The user said "The file doesn't need to exist; just attempt the Edit so I can see the permission prompt." So they EXPECT it may fail. Let me just attempt it.

Actually, the Edit tool description says: "You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing" - that's for notebooks. For files: "You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail."

So if I don't read the file first, the Edit call will fail with an error like "File has not been read yet. Read it first before writing to it." The user wants to see the permission prompt - the permission prompt happens when the tool call is attempted, regardless of whether the edit succeeds. So attempting Edit will surface the permission prompt.

But wait - should I read the file first? The user explicitly said the file doesn't need to exist and just to attempt the Edit. If I try to Read first and the file doesn't exist, that's fine too - Read will error. But the user just wants the Edit attempted.
